facts.claim: What 8-4 would be the first of
facts.value: First eight-win regular season since 2020 (8-2). Most regular-season wins since 2020, and the most in a 12-game regular season since 2019 (10-2). facts.claim: Jon Sumrall: when and how he got the job
facts.value: Florida hired Tulane's Jon Sumrall on Sunday, Nov. 30, 2025. ESPN reported a six-year deal averaging nearly $7.5 million a year. He replaced Billy Napier, who was fired Oct. 19, 2025; Billy Gonzales was interim coach and Florida finished 4-8. Sumrall was 42-11 in four seasons as a head coach (two at Troy, two at Tulane) when hired.
facts.sourceName: ESPN, 'Florida hires Tulane's Jon Sumrall as new football coach' (published Nov. 30, 2025 ET)
facts.how: read full story text through ESPN content API (content.core.api.espn.com/v1/sports/news/47151490); ESPN roster API lists coach Jon Sumrall, experience 0

facts.value: Sumrall has seven wins with a game and a bowl to play. Billy Napier's first team (2022) went 6-6 in the regular season and 6-7 overall. Dan Mullen's first team (2018) went 9-3 in the regular season and 10-3 overall. An eighth regular-season win would be the most by a first-year Florida coach since Mullen's nine. Regular-season records in other first years per ESPN's schedule data: 2015 10-2, 2011 6-6, 2005 8-3, 2002 8-4 (ESPN's API does not name the coach for those seasons; the names Jim McElwain, Will Muschamp, Urban Meyer and Ron Zook were NOT sourced here and need a check before use).

facts.claim: Is 'first in school history with back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons' supported?
facts.value: LIKELY, not verified at an official Florida source. FloridaGators.com could not be read (HTTP 403 from its bot wall to curl and to Playwright; WebFetch returns only page titles), so no game notes or record book were seen. What supports it: (1) Tampa Bay Times, Nov. 26, 2026: 'needs 20 yards to become the first Gator with consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons'; Sept. 4, 2026: 'a second consecutive 1,000-yard season — something never achieved at Florida'. (2) The list of Florida's twelve 1,000-yard seasons has no player in consecutive years. (3) ESPN data for 2004-2025 shows only Fason 2004, Gillislee 2012, Kelvin Taylor 2015 and Baugh 2025. Safe wording: attribute it ('would be the first Gator with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons, according to the Tampa Bay Times') or have the controller confirm against Florida's game notes.
facts.sourceName: Tampa Bay Times (bylines not shown to the fetch tool); SI 'Florida Gators on SI' (Cam Parker, Nov. 25, 2025); ESPN stats API

facts.claim: Every Florida 1,000-yard rushing season that could be documented
facts.value: Twelve seasons by ten players: Jimmy DuBose 1975 (1,307); Neal Anderson 1985 (1,034); Emmitt Smith 1987 (1,341) and 1989 (1,599); Errict Rhett 1991 (1,109) and 1993 (1,289); Fred Taylor 1997 (1,292); Earnest Graham 2002 (1,085); Ciatrick Fason 2004 (1,267); Mike Gillislee 2012 (1,152); Kelvin Taylor 2015 (1,035); Jadan Baugh 2025 (1,170). facts.claim: What a sixth win means for Florida State
facts.value: Bowl eligibility at 6-6. Florida State has not played in a bowl since the Orange Bowl on Dec. 30, 2023 (lost 63-3 to Georgia, finishing 13-1); it went 2-10 in 2024 and 5-7 in 2025. A loss makes it 5-7 again and a third straight losing season. NOTE: a win alone does not 'avoid a third straight losing season', as our game-time story says; at 6-6 that would depend on the bowl. By ESPN's schedule data FSU is 12-23 since the start of 2024; ESPN's prose says 12-24 'over the past three years', which matches only if the Orange Bowl loss is counted.

facts.claim: When and why Mike Norvell was dismissed
facts.value: Florida State fired Mike Norvell on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, the day after a 36-24 home loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5. He was 41-39 in seven seasons; ESPN reported a $50.3 million buyout. President Richard McCullough made the decision. Defensive coordinator Tony White and safeties coach Evan Cooper were also fired. CONFLICTS: our game-time story says 'fired on Nov. 2' (ESPN's UTC timestamp is Nov. 2; the firing was Sunday, Nov. 1 ET, and the school's release URL is dated 2026/11/1). Our Soothsayer column puts the money owed at $48.7 million; ESPN says $50.3 million.
facts.sourceName: ESPN (Andrea Adelson), 'Florida State fires Mike Norvell amid 3-5 football season'; Seminoles.com release URL
facts.how: full story read via ESPN content API (published 2026-11-02T02:22Z = 9:22 p.m. ET Nov. 1); a second ESPN story (Eli Lederman, Nov. 7) says Stockstill 'stepped into the interim role last Sunday'; the official release at seminoles.com/news/2026/11/1/florida-state-makes-football-leadership-change returned 403 and was not read

facts.value: Rick Stockstill, 68, Florida State's director of scouting for offense, was named interim coach on Nov. 1, 2026. He played quarterback at Florida State under Bobby Bowden (1977-81), was head coach at Middle Tennessee for 18 seasons (2006-23) and joined the FSU staff in 2024. He is 2-1 as interim: W 31-24 at Boston College (Nov. 7), W 16-10 at Pittsburgh (Nov. 13), L 10-28 to NC State (Nov. 21). The Boston College win was FSU's first road win since November 2023. Offensive coordinator Tim Harris Jr. calls plays; linebackers coach Ernie Sims is interim defensive coordinator.
facts.sourceName: ESPN (Andrea Adelson Nov. 1 and Nov. 2; Eli Lederman Nov. 7); ESPN coach record
facts.how: three ESPN stories read via content API (ids 50350481, 50359717, 50411545); ESPN core API lists FSU's coach as Rick Stockstill; results from schedule

facts.value: Florida State named Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann its head coach on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026 (school release time-stamped 11/23/2026 6:47 p.m.). ESPN reported a five-year deal and that he is expected to stay with Georgia through the season and postseason, so he does not coach Friday. He has been part of six national championships at Alabama and Georgia. Athletic director Jeff Purinton (hired in November) worked with him at Alabama. ESPN had reported on Sunday, Nov. 22 that the search was 'focused on' Schumann, which is the stale version in the tip sheet. tipSheetVerdicts.bullet: Florida is after its first eight-win regular season since 2020; a win helps its bowl position, with projections mentioning the Citrus, Gator and ReliaQuest bowls.
tipSheetVerdicts.note: True as worded: 8-2 in the 2020 regular season, no eight-win regular season since. Keep the word 'regular'; Florida won eight overall in 2024 with a bowl. Citrus, ReliaQuest and Gator are named by AP (Nov. 24); ESPN's two projections (Nov. 23) both say Gator Bowl vs SMU. Whether a win 'helps its bowl position' is the bowl researcher's call.

tipSheetVerdicts.bullet: Florida State needs a sixth win for bowl eligibility under interim coach Rick Stockstill; 'reportedly pursuing' Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann to replace fired coach Mike Norvell.
tipSheetVerdicts.note: First half verified (FSU is 5-6; Stockstill has been interim since Nov. 1 and is 2-1). Second half is stale: Florida State named Schumann head coach on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026; ESPN reports a five-year deal and that he stays with Georgia through the postseason. Norvell was fired Sunday, Nov. 1.

tipSheetVerdicts.bullet: Jadan Baugh needs about 20 yards to become the first player in school history with back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons.
tipSheetVerdicts.verdict: verified for the yardage (exactly 20: 980 per ESPN and NCAA.com); 'first in school history' is likely but unverified at an official Florida source
tipSheetVerdicts.note: FloridaGators.com was blocked. Supported by the Tampa Bay Times (Nov. 26) and by the list of twelve 1,000-yard seasons, none consecutive. Attribute the 'first' or have the controller check Florida's game notes.

deskFlagsInOurOwnPublishedStories: Our Nov. 24 Buddy Martin column says Baugh 'needs 19 yards'. ESPN and NCAA.com have him at 980, so it is 20. Three of our stories today say 20.

Our Nov. 23 Franz Beard story calls Schumann 'the grandson of Florida State's first football coach, Ed Williamson'. Florida State's release and ESPN say his grandfather is Jack Haskin, an assistant coach on the 1947 team.
Our game-time story today says Norvell 'was fired on Nov. 2'. ESPN says Sunday, which was Nov. 1; the school's release URL is dated Nov. 1.

Our stories give three openers for the line: 4.5 (Nov. 23), 5.5 (Behind the Sticks, today), and the game-time story cites BetMGM at 6.5. DraftKings opened 4.5 and is 6.5 now. Name the book and time whenever a number is printed.
Our Soothsayer column says FSU owes Norvell $48.7 million; ESPN reported a $50.3 million buyout on Nov. 1.
Our Soothsayer column says Baugh is 123 yards behind Tim Tebow on the career list; ESPN's totals make it 124 (2,947 minus 2,823). Unresolved by one yard.
Our game-time story says a win lets FSU 'avoid a third straight losing season'. A win makes FSU 6-6; a bowl loss would still leave it 6-7.
AP's recap of the Vanderbilt game gives Baugh 73 yards; ESPN's box score and the NCAA season total imply 75.
